# Welcome

You just rendered a PDF **without LaTeX**. The line `format: typst` in the
YAML header above told Quarto to use its bundled Typst engine. Rendering
should have taken about a second — that speed is the point.

Everything you already know about Quarto still applies: Markdown text,
R code chunks, YAML options. Typst only changes *how the PDF is produced*.

# How rendering works

When you press **Render**, this happens:

1. `knitr` runs your R chunks and produces Markdown.
2. Pandoc converts the Markdown to a `.typ` file (Typst source).
3. Quarto's bundled Typst compiler turns `.typ` into PDF.

You can inspect the intermediate Typst source — very useful for learning —
by adding `keep-typ: true` under the `typst:` key.

# R code works as usual

```{r}
#| label: first-chunk
#| echo: true
head(mtcars, 4)
```

And inline code too: the `mtcars` dataset has `r nrow(mtcars)` rows and
`r ncol(mtcars)` columns. Mean fuel efficiency is
`r round(mean(mtcars$mpg), 1)` mpg.

# The YAML options that matter

These go under `format: typst:` in the header:

| Option | Example | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `papersize` | `a4`, `us-letter`, `a5` | Page size |
| `margin` | `x: 2cm`, `y: 3cm` (or `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) | Margins |
| `fontsize` | `10pt`, `11pt` | Base font size |
| `mainfont` | `"Libertinus Serif"` | Body font (any font Typst can see) |
| `columns` | `2` | Multi-column body text |
| `toc` | `true` | Table of contents |
| `number-sections` | `true` | Numbered headings |
| `keep-typ` | `true` | Keep the intermediate `.typ` file |

# Exercises

Complete each exercise by editing **this file** and re-rendering.

## 🏋️ Exercise 1.1 — Make it yours

Change `author` to your real name, and change the `date` from `today` to a
fixed date such as `"2026-07-18"`. Re-render and check the title block.

## 🏋️ Exercise 1.2 — Page geometry

Change the paper size to `us-letter` and set asymmetric margins:
`left: 4cm`, `right: 2cm`, `top: 2.5cm`, `bottom: 2.5cm`.
(Replace the `x:` / `y:` shorthand.)

## 🏋️ Exercise 1.3 — Typography

Set `fontsize: 10pt` and `mainfont: "Libertinus Sans"` (a font bundled with
Typst). Notice the entire document switch to a sans-serif face.

## 🏋️ Exercise 1.4 — Look under the bonnet

Add `keep-typ: true`, re-render, and open the generated
`01-getting-started.typ` file in RStudio. Find where your heading
"Welcome" appears in Typst syntax. Don't worry about understanding it all
yet — that's Module 2.

::: {.callout-tip}
Solutions for all exercises are in `solutions/01-solutions.qmd`.
:::
